economic_question: What is the sign and bp distance of the same-date U.S. 10Y-minus-2Y Treasury spread from zero, how do recent movements decompose into its two yield legs, and can prior behavior contextualize movement without overstating the available history?
economic_relevance: Distinguish curve shape from movement and identify whether a changing spread reflects the short leg, the long leg, or both.
what_it_measures: Descriptive same-date yield difference, signed recent movement, path reversal and conditional prior-distribution context.
downstream_intended_use: Auditable market awareness and input to later separately authorized research.
input_selection: Phase 1 current direct processed outputs matching the greatest valid (FRED realtime_start, realtime_end, vintage) for each series/date; include every retained valid leg in the snapshot; inner-align dates for calculation.
alignment: Same economic date only; no forward fill, interpolation, alternate vintage fallback or calendar insertion; both source-null and absent-leg cases remain explicit.
grid_rationale: 1 is consecutive aligned observation movement; 3/5 test very short endpoint versus path behavior; 10 checks a longer short-history boundary. 21/63 are exploratory approximately monthly/quarterly observation scales for sensitivity, not calendar-month guarantees or production defaults. 5 and expanding-minimum-5 expose small-reference failure; no horizon is selected by this study.
numeric_policy: Decimal(str(stored percent value)); exact subtraction and percentage_point-to-bp primitive; no rounding, tolerance or epsilon for sign/ties. Compare Phase 1 binary-float derived values with tolerance 1e-10 percentage points only in validation, never for curve sign.
availability: Preserve actual raw publication timestamp if present; otherwise null/unknown. FRED realtime dates are vintage identity, not publication times. This is a current-vintage descriptive snapshot, not historical event-time replay.
state_policy: Research-only positive/zero/inverted sign descriptors have exact zero boundary. Near-flat, unusually steep, trend, anomaly and materiality states remain unclassified.
reference_policy: Level contexts exclude current; change rarity compares current absolute one-step movement to preceding changes only. Strict and weak empirical CDF endpoints expose ties without choosing a tie point estimate. No fallback or partial rolling windows.
limitations: Ten local aligned dates cannot establish long-history or multiple-environment behavior.
Synthetic cases test semantics and arithmetic, not observed historical frequency or predictive validity.
